question: The horrific events of 7 October saw Israeli women subjected to unprecedented violence by Hamas militiamen, including rape, mutilation and other abuse. Before being put to death 'women were subjected to gang violence that shattered their pelvises, their legs were torn apart, their vaginas torn apart with knives, their breasts removed and used as footballs’.

The manner and intensity of this violence reveals it to be mass femicide1. These were not isolated incidents but rather part of a premeditated plan to inflict maximum harm, highlighting a clear gender dimension in the atrocities. It is imperative that these acts be recognised as crimes against humanity and gender-based violence. Can the Vice-President / High Representative therefore say: 1.
Whether he will take a clear and decisive stance, formally recognising these events as mass femicide and condemning those responsible for their crimes?
What action he will take to investigate and recognise the events of 7 October as mass femicide, considering the evidence and testimonies of the atrocities suffered by Israeli women?

Whether he can help ensure that those responsible for such crimes against humanity and gender-based violence are identified, brought to justice and sentenced appropriately, in accordance with international law and the principles of justice and equality?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.7.2024) The High Representative/Vice-President (HR/VP) condemned the Hamas terrorist attacks on 7 October 2023 and the resulting killing of all civilians on several occasions1, and considers that all allegations and reports of sexual violence and other war crimes must be investigated and those responsible held accountable resolutely and without delay.
The HR/VP also strongly condemned all forms of sexual and gender-based violence, including femicide2, broadly understood as the killing of a woman or girl because of her gender.

The European Council, in its conclusions of 21-22 March 20243, called for independent investigations into all allegations of sexual violence, noting the report4 by the United Nations (UN) Special Representative on Sexual Violence in Conflict with grave concern, as well as the reports by the UN Special Rapporteur on violence against women and girls, its causes and consequences.

The European Council stated that violations of international humanitarian law need to be thoroughly and independently investigated and accountability ensured. Furthermore, the EU is committed to preventing and countering sexual and gender-based violence in all contexts in order to ensure full accountability and to combat impunity.
This is why, in 2022, the Commission proposed the first ever Directive combating violence against women and domestic violence5, which was adopted by the co-legislators on 14 May 2024.

The EU stands for multilateral governance and rule-based international cooperation guided by fundamental rights, universal values and respect to international law, and will continue to call for full access for independent investigations by the International Criminal Court and the Commission of Inquiry as the first step in ensuring justice and accountability.
Furthermore, gender equality is an important political priority for the EU and subsequently the EU remains committed to gender analysis and gender-responsive action, also in this context.
